Three python processes held 10.4, 10.7 and 15.6 GB resident - about 40 GB together - with 1695, 3215 and 7233 seconds of CPU burned. Killed.

THE CAUSE IS IN THE SCRIPT, not the machine. It materialised every study's bags before predicting:

    bags = [Study.from_directory(...).bags(...) for n in chosen]
    images = np.stack([b[0].numpy() for b in bags])

250 studies x 6 slots x 12 slices x 336^2 uint8 is 2.03 GB, and np.stack DUPLICATES it. At 448 px it is 3.6 GB and 7.2 GB stacked. Four members in sequence, each holding its own copy alive while the next was built.

THIS IS THE SAME FAILURE THE PROJECT ALREADY HAS A BEAD FOR. knee-7gr records a cache build and a trainer killed together by the OS under RAM pressure - 93.6 GB against a 63.7 GB memmap beside a 27 GB trainer - and the lesson written down then was that VRAM headroom had been checked carefully and system RAM had not been checked at all. I checked neither.

THE FIX IS THE ONE THE SUBMISSION PATH ALREADY USES: Submission.chunks streams STUDY_CHUNK studies at a time and never holds the split in memory. The gate should do the same, and should be run in the FOREGROUND with a timeout so a runaway cannot survive unattended.

THE REAL COST: not the CPU, but that the offline justification the submission policy requires still does not exist, and a night passed without it.
acceptance_criteria: A streamed gate that prices the 22-member and 24-member shapes on the same studies, bounded in memory and wall time.
notes:
A SECOND ORPHAN, AND A SHARPER LESSON THAN THE FIRST. 2026-08-15.

After killing the overnight processes I re-ran the gate in the FOREGROUND, believing that made it safe. The harness caps a foreground command at 10 minutes and SIGTERM'd it at the cap - and the python child SURVIVED. Twenty minutes later it was still holding 15.86 GB with 9,519 seconds of CPU, alongside a second orphan at 3.74 GB.

WHY: the command was `timeout 1500 uv run python ...`. The signal goes to the wrapper. `uv run` spawns python as a child, and on Windows that child is not in a process group that dies with its parent - so terminating the shell leaves a detached python holding every allocation it had.

CONSEQUENCES FOR HOW LONG WORK IS RUN HERE:
  - "run it in the foreground so it cannot run away" is FALSE under this harness. The 10-minute cap makes a foreground long job strictly WORSE than a background one: it is killed at the wrapper and orphaned at the child, with nothing left watching it.
  - killing by StartTime window is not enough. My first sweep matched 22:07:00-22:09:00 and reported zero survivors; the orphan that mattered had started later, from the foreground attempt.
  - the reliable check is CPU TIME, not age: a process 30 seconds old cannot hold 9,000 seconds of CPU, and that single comparison found both orphans immediately.

THE RULE THIS EARNS: for anything expected to exceed a few minutes, run it in the BACKGROUND with a hard `timeout` INSIDE the backgrounded command, and verify afterwards by CPU time rather than by trusting the exit. Two runaways in one night, and the second was created by the fix for the first.
close_reason: Streamed gate landed and ran: chunked reads, bounded memory, priced the 22- and 24-member shapes on the same studies (fusion +0.0001, router +0.0026). The orphan-process lesson is in the notes and now in bd memory.

title: Split the twelve findings by whether the LABEL or the MODEL is the bottleneck
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 on the 58 annotated studies, held out for the published members, zero GPU.

Two numbers per finding, against the SAME radiologist truth:
  REPORT = the report label itself used as a predictor (how much signal our supervision carries)
  MODEL  = the published 4-seed out-of-fold ensemble

  aggregate:  report 0.8639   model 0.8391

  finding             report   model    model-report
  Effusion            0.8137   0.9453     +0.1317
  Contusion           0.7470   0.8421     +0.0951
  Medial OA           0.9085   0.9504     +0.0419
  Synovitis           0.6953   0.7372     +0.0418
  Fracture            0.8549   0.8861     +0.0312
  Baker's             0.9330   0.9547     +0.0217
  ------------------------------------------------- the model BEATS its own labels above here
  PF OA               0.8790   0.8005     -0.0785
  Lateral OA          0.7892   0.7099     -0.0793
  Medial Meniscus     0.9435   0.8498     -0.0938
  MCL                 0.9762   0.8798     -0.0964
  ACL                 0.9841   0.8640     -0.1201
  Lateral Meniscus    0.8429   0.6497     -0.1932

'CEILING' IS THE WRONG WORD AND I WILL NOT USE IT: a model fitted on noisy labels CAN beat them, by seeing the image, and here it does on six of twelve. The report number is a REFERENCE for how much signal the supervision carries, not a bound.

THE SPLIT IS THE FINDING, and it assigns different work to different findings:

LABEL-BOTTLENECKED (model already beats the report): Effusion, Contusion, Synovitis, Medial OA, Fracture, Baker's. The reader is the weak part - the model is already correcting it from the image. A better label reader (knee-dbw) pays HERE and nowhere else.

MODEL-BOTTLENECKED (the report describes it well and the model cannot reproduce it): ACL (report 0.9841, model 0.8640), Lateral Meniscus (0.8429 -> 0.6497), MCL, Medial Meniscus, Lateral OA, PF OA. The signal IS in the label and the model fails to extract it from the pixels. Better labels cannot help these; showing the model more of the image might (knee-jk3, knee-ghd).

LATERAL MENISCUS IS THE LARGEST MODEL-SIDE GAP OF ALL TWELVE at -0.1932, which sharpens knee-yrg: its weakness is NOT a label artefact - the report reads it at 0.8429 - it is a VISION failure.

ACL IS THE SURPRISE. It is a large central structure the report describes almost perfectly (0.9841), and the model loses 0.12 to it. Size cannot be the explanation, so resolution is not the mechanism there; slice sampling (the ACL is oblique, and we sample 12 slices uniformly over a 0.20-0.80 band) is the candidate that fits - see knee-ghd.

CAVEAT, load-bearing: n=58, with 9-35 positives per label, so each per-label number carries a wide interval (Hanley-McNeil puts it near +/-0.17 in this regime). The SPLIT and the two largest gaps are the evidence; no single row should be planned around alone.
acceptance_criteria: An arm targeted at a MODEL-bottlenecked finding, and a label-reader change evaluated only on LABEL-bottlenecked ones.
notes: Downgraded P0 -> P1 as bead HYGIENE, not as a change of view. This is a FINDING plus a standing rule ('a label-reader change is only evaluated on the label-bottlenecked six; an imaging change on the other six'), and the work it implies is already carried by knee-1nn at P0. A finding that is recorded and acted on does not also need to occupy the critical queue.

title: Lateral-compartment findings are our weakest axis, and it is NOT the laterality flip
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 on the full corpus (4,407 studies, published 4-seed OOF, confident_v2), zero GPU.

THE PROFILE, with 95% bootstrap intervals:
  Lateral Meniscus 0.7981 +/-0.0159 (n=1114)   <- THE WEAKEST LABEL, never named as a target before
  PF OA            0.8165 +/-0.0121 (n=1988)
  MCL              0.8166 +/-0.0155 (n=758)
  Lateral OA       0.8215 +/-0.0138 (n=1082)
  ...
  Fracture         0.8923 +/-0.0187 (n=313)    <- THE BEST LABEL

THE LEDGER'S TARGET IS DEAD. 'MCL 0.755 and Fracture 0.784 -> 0.873 is worth +0.0173' was read off 881 studies with 62 Fracture positives. Fracture is our STRONGEST finding at corpus scale. label_power predicted this from the standard error alone; this is the confirmation.

THE ASYMMETRY, both pairs, far outside the intervals:
  Medial Meniscus - Lateral Meniscus = +0.0622
  Medial OA       - Lateral OA       = +0.0472

THE FLIP HYPOTHESIS IS REFUTED. We mirror left knees to a canonical side, and a mis-flip swaps medial for lateral; since medial positives outnumber lateral ~2:1, leakage from the big class into the small one would produce exactly this signature. It does not survive the split:
  source=tag        2203 studies   +0.0475 / +0.0369
  tag+geom AGREE    2105 studies   +0.0519 / +0.0331
The gap persists where the DICOM tag and the independent geometric rule AGREE - as confidently sided as a study can be. The dead zone is 72 studies (1.6%) and the two rules disagree on 30; far too few to move an AUC by 0.06.

(source=geometry shows +0.0851/+0.0586, larger - but that subgroup is UNMATCHED: its UNSIDED labels also score 0.8748 vs the tag subgroup's 0.8565, so those studies are simply easier. Directional at most.)

SO IT IS A TARGETING STATEMENT, NOT A FIX: lateral-compartment structures are genuinely harder or rarer and the normalisation is doing its job. Lifting the four weakest labels to 0.87 - a level two findings already reach - is worth +0.0189 on the mean, which clears the 1.5% bar.

MECHANISM CANDIDATES FOR WHY LATERAL IS HARDER (untested): fewer positives (1114 vs 2341 meniscus, 1082 vs 1612 OA); the lateral compartment sits nearer the edge of a 130 mm crop centred on the joint; lateral meniscus tears are smaller. The first is measurable against the label table, the second against the crop geometry - both cheap.
acceptance_criteria: An arm whose mechanism targets lateral-compartment visibility specifically, justified against the corpus ruler rather than the 881-study holdout.
notes: INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED 2026-08-14 by the out-of-fold oracle. This bead refuted the laterality flip as the cause of the medial/lateral asymmetry by splitting on HOW each study's side was decided. The oracle confirms it from the other direction: disabling our laterality normalisation makes a published member's agreement with its OWN recorded predictions catastrophically worse (max 0.638 against 0.067, mean 4x). So our mirroring reproduces theirs, and it is not silently wrong. The asymmetry stands as a property of the findings rather than of the flip.

title: [bug] A member's recorded reading rules are written by a constant and read by nobody
description:
MemberConfig carries crop_mm, band, group, slices AND a ReadingRules dict (order, lat, slot_fallback, decode_fill) - 'the four decisions that settle what a slice IS'. Grep says the ONLY site that mentions any of them outside members.py is member_record.py:179-182, which WRITES them. Nothing reads them.

BOTH ENDS ARE DECORATIVE:
  - the writer hardcodes {'order':'normal','lat':'centre','slot_fallback':False,'decode_fill':'nearest'} rather than reading what the run actually used
  - the server ignores the record anyway: submission.py:93 builds SlotReader(image_size=max(read.sizes)), so crop_mm and band fall to the module constants (130.0, 0.20-0.80) for every member, and Laterality() takes its default

CONSEQUENCE: a member fitted under a different crop, band or laterality rule would be served under ours and NOTHING would notice - no fingerprint moves (it feeds noise), no witness moves (it replays the training path). This is the exact shape of the defect class that has already cost this project repeatedly: a value recorded in a config while the consumer reads a constant.

IT IS LATENT, NOT ACTIVE (2026-08-14): the published members' own checkpoints declare crop_mm 130.0, band '0.20,0.80', img 336, slices 12, group 3, pool cls_mean and the identical rules dict, so today every served member agrees with the constant by luck. The bug is that nothing would tell us when that stops being true - and the whole point of the reading-rules record was to make members that differ in reading SAFE to mix.
design: SlotReader and Laterality already take their values as constructor arguments; the missing piece is that Ensemble/Submission build ONE pipeline for a pixel group instead of one per member's recorded reading. Either honour the record per member, or delete the fields - a record nothing enforces is worse than no record, because it reads as a guarantee.
acceptance_criteria: Either a member declaring a non-default crop_mm/band/lat is demonstrably served under it, or the fields are gone.

title: [bug] loadcheck reported all six members FORWARD FAILED and all six had loaded fine
description:
The probe called package.load(...) and DISCARDED the return value, so the models dict it then indexed was empty and every member died on models[member.identifier] - a KeyError of the member's own name, logged as 'FORWARD FAILED <name>'. The weights had all loaded cleanly (223/223 per member).

This is the fourth harness-not-idea failure this week and the most expensive kind: the probe exists precisely to tell us which members work on a T4, and it answered 'none of them' for a reason that was entirely its own.

ALSO FIXED: it accumulated every member on the card. It now holds one resident at a time and empties the cache between, because 22 members on a 16 GB T4 would fail for a reason that has nothing to do with any member.

STILL UNKNOWN, and this is what the re-run buys: whether the members forward and CHUNK on a T4 under fp16/bf16/fp32, which is the question three lost submissions could not answer.
acceptance_criteria: A loadcheck log with per-member 'ok' lines and the three-precision chunk timings, which nothing has yet produced.

title: find_kit spent 248 seconds walking the competition mount
description:
MEASURED by the free loadcheck kernel on 2026-08-14: 't=248.2s kit located at /kaggle/input/datasets/dimiturnt/kneemri-kit/kneemri_src'. Four minutes before a line of ours ran, in EVERY kernel - all seven carried the same copy.

CAUSE: Path('/kaggle/input').rglob('kneemri/model.py') descends into the competition mount, which holds one directory per study and one per series beneath that, and stats every DICOM on the way.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND TIDINESS: the Efficiency Prize scores TOTAL RUNTIME, and this was our largest single expense - larger than any model choice we have argued about.

FIXED in 35140de: pruned by directory name (train_series/test_series/train_images/test_images) and bounded by depth, in all seven kernels. UNVERIFIED - the next kernel run of any kind will print its own t= line and settle it, at no cost.
acceptance_criteria: A kernel log whose 'kit located at' line is under ~20s.

title: Per-label combine: the reachable half of what the oracle prices
description:
THE GAP. The metric is the unweighted mean of twelve INDEPENDENT per-label AUCs, so the correct combine is per-label. We do a flat rank-average of every member for every label (Ensemble.combine). The only other thing that exists is member_curve.oracle, which picks the best member PER LABEL USING THE ANSWERS - a ceiling that can never be shipped. Between the flat average and the cheat there is nothing.

WHY IT MIGHT PAY. The ledger has MCL at 0.755 and Fracture at 0.784 against Baker's 0.896; lifting those two alone to 0.873 is +0.0173 on the mean, above the 1.5% bar and larger than whole-stack. If any member is materially better on the two weak labels, a flat 22-way average dilutes it by construction.

WHY IT MIGHT NOT, AND THE TRAP. Selecting per label ON the holdout that reports the number is selection optimism, and this holdout has 62 Fracture positives - split in half for an honest estimate, 31. The in-sample number will look good whether or not the strategy is real. So the deliverable is not a per-label combine; it is a per-label combine WITH the split-half estimator that says whether it survives being chosen on data it is not scored on. top-k where k = all members IS the flat rank-average, so the k curve carries its own matched control under the same estimator.

ZERO GPU: pure arithmetic over the arrays HoldoutPredictions.cached returns.
design: LabelCombine(scores): ranking() orders members per label by AUC on given studies; applied() rank-averages the top-k per label into one table; halves() splits studies for the honest estimator; honest() fits the ranking on one half and scores the other, both ways; curve() reports in-sample beside split-half for every k, with k=n as the matched flat-average control.
acceptance_criteria: A k curve where the split-half estimate at some k beats the split-half estimate at k=n by more than the noise floor - or a recorded refutation that it does not.
notes:
FIRST MEASUREMENT 2026-08-14, on the full corpus, zero GPU - and it is the NULL CASE, which is the right first test.

Ran on the published members' own out-of-fold predictions: 4 seeds x 4,407 studies (see the full-corpus ruler bead). Labels confident_v2.

  seed 0 0.8390   seed 1 0.8389   seed 2 0.8384   seed 3 0.8391
  flat 4-seed rank-average 0.8474

  top-1 per label:  in-sample 0.8419   split-half 0.8403
  top-2 per label:  in-sample 0.8462   split-half 0.8450
  top-3 per label:  in-sample 0.8471   split-half 0.8468
  top-4 per label:  in-sample 0.8474   split-half 0.8475  (= the flat rank-average)

PER-LABEL SELECTION LOSES MONOTONICALLY HERE, and it should: these four members are SEED TWINS of one recipe, so 'which member is best on MCL' is pure sampling noise and selecting on it only shrinks the ensemble. Cost of the strategy at k=1 is -0.007.

WHAT THIS BUYS: the estimator is CALIBRATED. It refuses to reward selection where there is nothing to select, and the in-sample column shows the +0.0016 optimism it stripped at k=1 - which is the failure mode the whole split-half design exists to prevent, caught working on a case whose answer is known in advance.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW: anything about DIVERSE members. The mechanism argument was always about members differing in resolution, pooling, slot scheme - seed twins are precisely the case where per-label combining cannot help. The real test still needs our own members' holdout predictions, and that still needs the prediction cache filled once on a GPU.

title: Our encoder reads slices and pools them - depth is an axis we throw away
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-14, prompted by the owner asking whether a video model would help.

WHAT WE DO NOW: DINOv2 encodes each slice INDEPENDENTLY and the slot embedding is an elementwise max over them. Inter-slice structure - that a tear continues across three slices while noise does not - is never modelled. Pooling is the only thing joining them.

TWO OF OUR OWN MEASUREMENTS SAY THAT AXIS CARRIES SIGNAL:
  - depth spread across windows is 0.036, larger than every method change this project has measured put together (knee-ghd)
  - whole-stack reading bought +0.0147, the single largest change we have, purely from seeing every depth in one pass rather than one sampled window

An MRI stack is a volume, which is the structure video encoders model natively rather than pool away.

PRIOR ART, gathered 2026-08-14 (see sources in the interpretation): V-JEPA outperforms VideoMAE on ultrasound video, with frozen-encoder gains up to 3.4% at full data and 8.35% at 10% of it; V-JEPA 2.1 is reported to nearly triple pretrained performance against earlier backbones. Also relevant and possibly a better fit: large-scale multi-sequence MRI pretraining (Nature Biomedical Engineering 2026) - a domain foundation model rather than a video one.

THE HONEST CAVEAT: ultrasound video is genuinely TEMPORAL and MRI depth is not. A video encoder pretrained on motion may transfer to a spatial axis, or may not, and nothing measured here says which. That is the first thing to test, and it is cheap to test frozen (embeddings + our existing head, which is what head_trial does).

COST: a new encoder family, a cache rebuild if the read geometry changes, and T4 inference budget. Gate it behind a frozen-encoder probe before any fine-tuning.

title: predict_groups decodes the whole split once PER PIXEL GROUP - three groups is three decodes
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-14 in our own dry run, which printed it plainly - and which I then quoted as evidence the path WORKED without ever saying what it cost. 60 studies, three pixel groups: 'studies 1-48: decode 12s' appears three times over, once per group.

Ensemble.predict_groups calls chunks_for(members, slices) once per group and each call decodes every study again. Decode is the I/O-bound half on a Kaggle host with four CPUs (12 ms per DICOM slice), so N groups costs N times the decode wall-clock. With res392 at 392 px, the 336 px members, and the v3 LoRA member at 224 px, that is THREE full decodes of the hidden test set.

IT ALSO DECIDES WHICH MEMBERS CAN BE IN AN ENTRY AT ALL. The fusion kernel serves one decode, so it drops every member outside the largest pixel group - our two strongest members among them - because one decode cannot produce two sizes. That is why the 0.894 family cannot currently carry res392 (0.8523).

THE OBVIOUS FIX HAS A REAL HAZARD. Decode once at the LARGEST size and resample down per group. But a member's fingerprint and witness were recorded under pixels produced by decoding AT its own size, and a resampled 448 -> 392 is not bit-identical to a native 392 decode. The change must be verified against witness_check before it ships, and a mismatch there is the check working rather than an obstacle.

WORTH IT: 3x decode becomes 1x, and one entry could then carry members of different resolutions - the only way the two strongest members we own can appear beside the twenty published ones.
notes:
THE OFFLINE GATE RAN AND IT REFUSES THE 24-MEMBER ENTRY. 2026-08-15, CPU only, no slot.

48 fold-0 holdout studies - honest for both sides, since our members never trained on them and the published members' predictions there are genuinely out of fold:

  their 20 alone                 0.8355
  22-member shape (theirs + 2)   0.8577     <- +0.022 from our first two
  24-member shape (theirs + 4)   0.8578     <- +0.0001 from the next two

  calibrated_targets   alone 0.8525
  sliceattn            alone 0.8540
  res392_ws            alone 0.8383
  intensity392_ws      alone 0.8369

SO ADDING OUR TWO STRONGEST-ON-PAPER MEMBERS BUYS NOTHING. One ten-thousandth, against a 0.0053 noise floor. The policy bar is a predicted gain over 0.894 and this predicts no gain at all, so the entry does not get a slot.

WHY THIS IS NOT A CONTRADICTION OF res392 BEING OUR BEST MEMBER. Its recorded holdout is 0.8523 and here it scores 0.8383 - but n=48 puts a per-member interval near +/-0.03, so the individual numbers cannot be ranked at this size and should not be. The 22-vs-24 comparison is PAIRED on the same studies and is the only number here worth acting on.

THE MECHANISM THAT FITS: redundancy, not weakness. Our first two members buy +0.022 over the published twenty; the next two buy nothing. res392 and intensity392 are both whole-stack members differing mainly in resolution and intensity handling, so they plausibly fail the same way as calibrated_targets and sliceattn already in the set. That is the same lesson the ledger already holds from the other direction - a third member of OUR OWN recipe bought nothing (0.882 -> 0.882) while a different recipe bought +0.006 - and it is DIVERSITY that pays, not member quality.

WHAT WOULD CHANGE THE ANSWER: the same comparison at several hundred studies rather than 48, which needs a GPU pass rather than a CPU one. Until then the honest statement is "no evidence of gain", not "proven useless".

THE FUSION CODE CHANGE STAYS REGARDLESS. Filtering by READ rather than by pixel group is correct - it was dropping members for a reason that had expired - and it costs nothing when the members it admits turn out not to help.

title: A stale kit spent a slot and scored 0.500, and the fix for that exact OOM was already committed
description:
2026-08-13, measured on the leaderboard. The kneemri-efficient entry scored 0.500 - chance, the fallback's constant table.

THE CAUSE IS FULLY IDENTIFIED AND IT IS NOT A MODELLING ONE. The mounted kneemri-kit was built 2026-08-12 09:46 UTC. The commit that bounds the forward pass by IMAGES rather than studies - 9f31b35, 'ensemble: bound the forward by IMAGES, which is what OOM'd the T4 and cost a slot' - landed 2026-08-12 13:11 UTC, three and a half hours LATER. So the kit predates the fix for the exact failure it then reproduced: whole-stack members send studies x slots x 12 images instead of x 3, four times the peak activation, and 16 GB of T4 is not enough. The run wrote no submission and the fallback scored 0.500.

TWO SLOTS HAVE NOW BEEN SPENT ON THE SAME OOM, and the second was spent AFTER the fix existed, because nothing tied the code on Kaggle to the code in the repo. That is the whole argument for knee-<kit-drift>: build_kit now stamps the commit and kernel_run logs it (the trained run's log reads 'kit 5ba86ee'), but a PRE-SUBMISSION CHECK comparing the mounted kit to HEAD still does not exist, and that is what would have stopped this one.

WHAT IS STILL UNMEASURED: the efficiency configuration itself. Two whole-stack members at 2 passes/study is untested on the leaderboard - the 0.882 pair predates these members. Re-running it on a current kit is cheap and remains worth a slot.

WHAT IS NOT AT RISK: the trained v6 entry submitted at 23:17 ran on kit 5ba86ee, which carries both the OOM fix and Member.precision.

title: Nothing checks that the code mounted on Kaggle is the code we think it is
description:
COST INCURRED 2026-08-13, on a live submission. The kneemri-kit dataset was built 2026-08-12 09:46 and HEAD was 54 commits ahead of it. The efficiency entry therefore ran WITHOUT Member.precision, so calibrated_targets_s2026 - a bf16 member - was served under fp16 autocast on a T4, whose exponent range is narrower than bf16's. Found while the kernel was already running; too late to stop.

THE ASYMMETRY IS THE BUG. Members are versioned (a dataset version per upload), kernels are versioned (a version per push), and the CODE BETWEEN THEM was not versioned at all - a kernel run printed nothing about which commit it held, and no local command could tell either.

DONE: build_kit now stamps {commit, dirty} into kneemri_src/kit.json and logs it at build time.

STILL OPEN, and it is the half that would have caught this:
  1. kernel_run should LOG the kit's commit at startup, so a run's own output names the code that made it. Right now the stamp exists but nothing reads it.
  2. A pre-submission check should refuse - or at least warn loudly - when the kit's stamped commit is not HEAD. The three existing checks (arm_check, ledger_check, witness_check) each exist for a failure that already happened; this is the fourth, and it happened tonight.

WHY WITNESS_CHECK DID NOT CATCH IT: the witness compares predictions from the TRAINING path on this machine against the member's recorded witness, and it passed - because it runs against the local tree, which was current. Nothing compares the local tree to the MOUNTED one.

title: Holdout predictions are recomputed on every analysis, so offline work needs a GPU it should not need
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-13. member_curve.main calls HoldoutPredictions.predict for every member on every invocation, and nothing is written to disk. The consequence is structural, not a slowdown: THE ANALYSIS HALF OF THIS PROJECT IS GPU-GATED FOR NO REASON.

kneemri/holdout_predictions.py:27 already names the split - 'the half that needs a GPU, a cache and 90 seconds' - and says keeping the curve a pure function of arrays is what makes it testable. The cache in that sentence does not exist. Only the images are cached (images_336px_12sl.npy and friends); no member's probabilities are.

WHAT IT COSTS TODAY: every paired-floor run, every oracle, every subset search, every per-label weighting experiment re-runs the encoder over the holdout for N members. With the card busy - which it is, and which is a normal state, not an exception - none of it can run at all, even though all of it is numpy over arrays of shape (881, 12).

THE FIX: key each member's holdout probabilities by everything that changes them and write them beside the image caches. Key must include the checkpoint's identity (name + size + mtime_ns, so a retrained member under the same name MISSES), the holdout's identity (a hash of the study identifiers actually scored, so a split change misses), and the reading policy (window starts + width + size, the view set, the precision). Anything omitted from that key is the project's recurring defect - a value travels per-run while a consumer reads a constant - in its tenth costume.

WHAT IT UNBLOCKS IMMEDIATELY: knee-3vh (paired floor), the oracle/diversity curve under midranks, and the offline gate knee-uff requires before any submission - all become runnable with the GPU busy.
close_reason:
Built and gated 2026-08-13. PredictionCache (kneemri/prediction_cache.py) stores each member's holdout probabilities beside the image caches; HoldoutPredictions.cached reads from it and reaches the encoder, the download and the GPU ONLY on a miss; HoldoutSlab (kneemri/holdout_slab.py) makes the several-GB holdout copy lazy so a fully-cached run touches no pixels either - asserted directly in the test rather than inferred, because otherwise it would pass on any machine that happens to have a free card.

THE KEY carries the checkpoint's name, size and mtime_ns, a hash of the studies actually scored, the window (starts, width, size), the view set and the precision - each with its own partition in test_key. --refresh is the escape hatch and still writes.

WHAT REMAINS: the cache is EMPTY. Populating it costs one GPU pass per member and the card is not ours today; after that first pass, every paired interval, oracle, subset search and per-label weighting on this holdout runs with no GPU at all.

title: Our best member changed TWO things and the ledger credited one
description:
FOUND 2026-08-13 while preparing res392 for a re-run. res392_ws_s2026 is the best member this project has produced (0.8523) and its ledger row has read '336 -> 392 px, +0.0066, clears the floor' since 2026-08-12. The checkpoints' own recorded options say otherwise:

    member                   backbone lr   cache   read
    wholestack_s2026 (ctrl)     8e-6        336     336
    res392_ws_s2026             4e-5        448     392
    intensity392_ws_s2026       4e-5        448     392

FIVE TIMES THE ENCODER RATE, on top of the resolution change. And the rate alone was independently measured at +0.0044 in the windowed era (knee-3om) - most of the +0.0066 now attributed to resolution. If that transfers, resolution alone is about +0.002, comfortably INSIDE the 0.0053 floor and not a finding.

IT MAY NOT TRANSFER: +0.0044 was measured under windowed reading before whole-stack existed, so the rate's value under the current recipe is genuinely unknown. What is NOT uncertain is that this row cannot be read as a resolution result.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE ROW: res392 is in the all-ours package, is quoted in the running total as '+0.0251 against the original control', and knee-jk3 lists '336 px for findings a few voxels across' as one of four causes that PAID. That last claim now rests on a confounded arm.

THE CLEAN TEST IS ONE ARM: 392 px at 8e-6, matched to the control's rate. experiments/arms/resolution.sh now takes the rate as its third argument (default 4e-5, so a plain re-run reproduces the member on disk):
    bash experiments/arms/resolution.sh 392 448 8e-6

Also fixed in the same arm while there: --vram-gb 28 -> 26 (a cap close to physical permits the paging it exists to prevent) and --patience 3.
acceptance_criteria: 392 px at 8e-6 against wsfold0_e6 = 0.8457. Resolution either survives on its own or our best member is mostly a rate change already measured.
notes:
SWEPT EVERY MEMBER 2026-08-13, and res392 is the ONLY genuine case - worth recording, because a systematic confound would be a much larger problem than one row.

Compared every checkpoint's recorded options against its own stated control. Filtering the diff noise - train_size None->0, lora_rank None->0, per_label_loss None->False are fields added AFTER the control was trained, so the control has no value rather than a different one - what remains:

    res392_ws          resolution AND backbone_lr 5x    CONFOUNDED (this bead)
    intensity392_ws    intensity_aug only, against res392 as its control   matched
    slices16_ws        slices 16                        clean
    sliceattn          slice_pooling attend             clean
    extended_ws        scheme extended                  clean
    schedule_8         epochs 8                         clean
    calibrated_targets calibrated targets               clean
    lora v3small       lora_rank AND rate, against dinov3_224 - and that arm's HEADER already states the confound cannot be removed, because a frozen-base run and a fine-tuned run cannot share a backbone rate

The 24-epoch arms (rank24, lr5x, deep24, large24) differ from wholestack_s2026 on several axes but were never compared to it: they belong to the earlier baseline era and were matched among themselves.

SO THE LEDGER IS OTHERWISE SOUND. One row credits one cause when two changed; every other arm varies one thing against its own control, or states the confound it cannot remove.

title: The graded targets are miscalibrated: we train on 0.68 where the radiologist agrees 38% of the time
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 against the only ground truth we have - the 57 fully-annotated studies in train.csv (696 cells, all twelve labels annotated). For each report-derived level, how often the RADIOLOGIST agrees the finding is present:

  assigned  measured   95% CI            n     assigned inside CI?
    0.08     0.041     [0.013, 0.068]   196    NO
    0.28     0.136     [0.085, 0.186]   177    NO
    0.68     0.378     [0.282, 0.474]    98    NO
    0.82     0.688     [0.611, 0.764]   141    NO
    0.94     0.958     [0.912, 1.004]    72    yes

FOUR OF FIVE SIT OUTSIDE THE INTERVAL, all four TOO HIGH, and worst in the middle: we train the model to predict 0.68 for cells that are positive 38% of the time, and 0.28 for UNK cells that are positive 14% of the time.

THIS ALSO SETTLES knee-mxj's cheap first test, and in the strong direction. The three YES levels are NOT LLM certainty noise - agreement runs 0.38 / 0.69 / 0.96, monotone across a span of 0.58, which is enormous next to any effect this project has measured.  is constant per verdict (NO 0.85, UNK 0.05, YES 0.95), so it is NOT what separates them; the levels carry real per-study information about the quantity the competition scores.

WHERE IT ENTERS: targets.py:73 reads the value straight from the label table's own column, so the map lives in the CSV rather than in our code. Recalibration is a load-time remap - no reader work, no new labels, no extra compute.

THE HONEST CAVEAT, and it is a real one: those 57 studies are our only UNBIASED ruler. Using them to set training targets spends some of that independence, and n per level is 72-196 so the exact values must not be fitted. What is robust is the ORDERING and the DIRECTION and SIZE of the miscalibration; the fix should move the targets toward the measured rates, not onto them.
design: A monotone remap applied where Targets reads the column, so the label table stays the reader's output and the calibration stays ours and reviewable. Keep the current map available so the change is an arm rather than a silent redefinition of every past number.
acceptance_criteria: One arm with recalibrated targets against wsfold0_e6 = 0.8457. The mechanism predicts the gain concentrates where the miscalibration is largest - the middle level and UNK - so a uniform shift would refute the story even if the mean moves.
notes:
RESULT 2026-08-13. Peak 0.8495 at epoch 6 against the control's 0.8457 at epoch 6 - same recipe otherwise. MEAN +0.0038, which is INSIDE the 0.0053 floor: directional, not a finding.

THE MECHANISM PREDICTION FAILED IN DIRECTION. The arm predicted the gain would concentrate where the miscalibration is largest - MCL and Effusion, the labels most skewed toward the badly-valued 0.68 - and that PF OA, already nearly calibrated, would barely move. Measured:
    PF OA            +0.0198   largest gain of the twelve, predicted to be the smallest
    Fracture         +0.0170
    Medial Meniscus  -0.0136
    Contusion        +0.0115
    Lateral Meniscus +0.0110
    Effusion         -0.0085   predicted to move most, moved the wrong way
    MCL              +0.0045   predicted to move most, barely moved
That is not a uniform shift, which is what the falsifier warned about - it is ANTI-correlated with the prediction, which is worse for the story.

BUT THE TEST CANNOT RESOLVE IT. Not one of the twelve deltas clears its own label's 95% sampling interval, so the per-label pattern is UNREAD rather than refuted. At 62-533 positives per label a knob-sized effect is simply not measurable on one holdout, and this arm's whole falsifiable claim was per-label.

SO THE HONEST STATE: the change is free, mechanism-sound in its derivation (four of five assigned values sit outside their measured intervals), worth +0.0038 directionally, and its mechanism is unconfirmed. Keep --calibrated-targets available; do not plan around it; do not quote the per-label pattern in either direction.

THIS IS THE STRONGEST ARGUMENT YET FOR knee-3vh, the paired floor. Two arms scored on the SAME 881 studies share their sampling error, so the paired interval is far tighter than the unpaired one used here - it is the difference between 'unread' and an answer, and it costs a bootstrap over cached predictions.

title: Epochs 7-11 of a 12-epoch run have never won: stop on patience, not on a fixed count
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 from the metrics files, no GPU spent. The 12-epoch OneCycle peaks at epoch 6 and then does nothing for five more:

  epoch   6     7     8     9    10    11
  AUC  .8457 .8410 .8394 .8395 .8391 .8394

Same shape in every DINOv2 whole-stack arm - wsfold0, res392, sliceattn, slices16, extended_ws and wholestack_fold1 ALL peak at epoch 6 of 12. We keep the best-epoch checkpoint, so those five epochs produce weights that are thrown away: at 234 s/epoch that is ~19 minutes per arm, ~42% of its wall-clock.

THE SLOW ANNEAL IS STILL WORTH IT, so this is not 'run fewer epochs'. OneCycle is defined over total_steps, so an 8-epoch run compresses the whole schedule rather than truncating it - and measured head to head the 8-cycle is AHEAD early (e0 .7510 vs .7393, e2 .8163 vs .8104) and BEHIND at the end (.8429 vs .8457). Compressing costs 0.0028. The fix is to keep the 12-epoch SHAPE and stop early inside it.

A FIXED STOP WOULD BE WRONG, and the exceptions carry the mechanism: intensity392 peaks at 9, dinov3_v3small at 11 of 15, dinov3_224 at 8. Heavier augmentation and a different encoder both converge LATER - which is what you would expect, since both make the fit harder. A blanket 'stop at 7' would have cost exactly those arms.

SO: patience-based early stopping. Stop after N epochs with no improvement on the holdout, N=3. On the DINOv2 whole-stack recipe that stops at epoch 9 and saves 2-3 epochs; on intensity392 (peak 9) and the DINOv3 arms it runs to the end and costs nothing. Adaptive, and it cannot change any recorded best because the best-epoch checkpoint is what we already keep.
design: Trainer already tracks the best score for checkpointing, so patience is a counter beside it plus an early return. The schedule must still be constructed for the FULL epoch count so the anneal shape is unchanged - stopping early must not become compressing.
acceptance_criteria: A --patience flag, defaulting off so no existing arm's meaning changes; one arm re-run with it reproduces the same best epoch and best score as its recorded run while doing fewer epochs.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED and validated against recorded history, no GPU spent. kneemri/patience.py + --patience, default 0 (off) so no arm in the ledger changes meaning.

VALIDATION IS A REPLAY, which is stronger than the single re-run this bead asked for: every one of the 12 arms with a metrics file was replayed through the policy. At patience=3 all 12 keep EXACTLY their recorded best score, six of them stop 2 epochs early, and the late-peaking arms (intensity392 at 9, dinov3_v3small at 11 of 15, dinov3_224 at 8, schedule_8 at 7) correctly run to the end.

THE SWEEP, and it corrects this bead's own 42% claim:
  patience=1   40% of epochs saved   BEST LOST IN 6 OF 12 RUNS, worst -0.0805
  patience=2   15%                   none lost
  patience=3    9%                   none lost
  patience=4    4%                   none lost

42% was the epochs AFTER the peak; patience cannot recover those because it has to OBSERVE the staleness first. The real saving is 9-15%.

THE CLIFF AT 1 IS THE INTERESTING PART: the holdout curve is not monotonic - it dips and recovers - so a one-epoch budget stops on a dip and throws away 0.08. Two survives this history with ZERO margin; three has a margin of one epoch. Recommend --patience 3 in arms: 9% of wall-clock, free, and one step away from the cliff rather than standing on it.
close_reason: Implemented, swept and validated by replaying all 12 recorded runs: patience=3 preserves every recorded best exactly while stopping six arms 2 epochs early. Default is off.

title: The paired floor: per-label deltas are unreadable without it, and four arms were misread already
description:
Every per-label delta this project has quoted was read bare. Calibrated against each label's own 95% interval (kneemri.label_power, now wired into run_comparison), four arms with unrelated mechanisms each 'improved' Fracture by +0.012 to +0.037 against an interval of +/-0.061 - extended_ws, intensity392, slices16 and schedule_8. Not four mechanisms. One noisy label.

BUT THE UNPAIRED BOUND IS TOO CONSERVATIVE, and that is why this is a task and not a done thing. Two arms scored on the SAME 881 studies share their sampling error, so the delta between them has a far tighter interval than either AUC does. An unmarked delta is currently UNREAD, not refuted - and some of them are certainly real.

THE MEASUREMENT: bootstrap over studies on cached holdout predictions - resample the 881 studies with replacement, recompute both arms' per-label AUCs on each resample, and take the interval of the DIFFERENCE. No training, no GPU beyond the inference we already do for member_curve.

WHY IT IS WORTH A P1: it decides which of the ledger's per-label claims survive, and per-label is how every falsifiable arm in this project states its prediction. Without it a mechanism argument cannot be checked against its own evidence at knob size.
acceptance_criteria: run_comparison marks a delta against the PAIRED interval, and the arms already run are re-read against it - stating plainly which previously-reported per-label findings do not survive.
notes:
INHERITS TWO UNANSWERED PER-LABEL PREDICTIONS, which is the concrete case for running it:
  knee-8ev extended slots - predicted the gain concentrates in MCL and LCL (the coronal-read labels). Measured MCL +0.0056 against a +/-0.040 unpaired interval: unread.
  knee-bot calibrated targets - predicted it concentrates where miscalibration is largest, MCL and Effusion. Measured PF OA +0.0198 as the LARGEST gain, which is anti-correlated with the prediction, and not one of twelve deltas clears.
Both arms are already trained and on disk. The paired interval is about eleven times tighter than the unpaired bound and needs one inference pass over members we already have - it turns two 'unread' verdicts into answers without a single training hour.

title: Oracle ensemble: measure the CEILING of member combination before building another member
description:
Stolen from biohub_kaggle 7b982b0, which advanced every cell by its GROUND-TRUTH velocity to ask what a perfect Kalman filter could rescue - answer 0 of 35 - and closed a whole lever for the cost of a diagnostic instead of an implementation.

OUR VERSION. On the fold-0 holdout, with member predictions we have already paid for:
  (a) PER-LABEL ORACLE: for each of the twelve labels take the ranks of whichever member scores it best. That is the ceiling of ANY per-label member weighting scheme.
  (b) PER-STUDY ORACLE: for each study, the best ranking any member gives it. A looser ceiling on any combination rule at all.
Compare both against the best subset member_curve finds by plain rank-averaging.

WHY IT IS THE RIGHT NEXT MEASUREMENT. Diversity, not member quality, is what moved our leaderboard - five weak members scored 0.888 and two members 0.021 better EACH scored 0.882. Every plan we have (v3 as a diversity member, extended slots, LoRA) is a bet that combination has headroom left, and none of them has ever been priced against a ceiling. If the per-label oracle sits near the plain average, member weighting is dead before it is written and the diversity story is exhausted; if it sits far above, weighting is the cheapest gain on the board and no new member is needed to collect it.

COSTS NO TRAINING - inference over the holdout for members already on disk, the same pass member_curve makes.
design: Extend kneemri.member_curve, which already loads holdout predictions per member and groups by cache. The oracle is argmax over members of the per-label AUC, not a fit - no risk of the oracle itself overfitting beyond the obvious (it is an upper bound BY CONSTRUCTION and must be reported as one, never as a score we could achieve).
acceptance_criteria: Two numbers against the plain best subset: per-label oracle and per-study oracle, both stated as ceilings. The verdict is which of 'build another member' and 'weight the members we have' is worth wall-time.
notes:
LOWERED BACK TO P1 2026-08-13. I raised it to P0 this morning on the grounds that it would settle whether diversity dominates quality. experiments/README.md had already settled that across six leaderboard entries - a third member of our own recipe bought nothing while a different recipe bought +0.006 - so the oracle is not answering an open strategic question and should not have jumped the queue.

IT IS STILL WORTH RUNNING, for the narrower thing it actually measures: how much headroom is left in the members we ALREADY have. The README says 'build differently-failing members'; the oracle says whether per-label weighting of the current set is worth anything before another member is trained. That is useful and it is not urgent.

title: The witness tolerance was tighter than bf16's own epsilon
description:
witness_check carried TOLERANCE = 2e-3, inherited from the fingerprint and documented as 'above GPU noise' - true when training ran in float32 or float16, false the day bf16 landed. bfloat16 keeps float32's exponent and spends seven bits on the mantissa, so its eps is 2^-7 = 7.8e-3, FOUR TIMES the gate.

The check would refuse every bf16 member, correctly by its own rule and wrongly in fact. A gate that cries wolf is a gate someone switches off before a real refusal arrives - and this one runs as step 2b of prepare_submission.sh, so it blocks entries.

MEASURED on sliceattn_s2026 (fp16 witness) re-derived in float32: max 2.34e-3 over all 96 numbers, mean 4.3e-4, median 2.7e-4, nothing above 1e-2, every label moved about equally. The shape of arithmetic noise. The four reading defects this check exists for moved predictions 0.05-0.5 and concentrated in some labels while sparing others.
design: tolerance(precision) derives the bound from torch.finfo(dtype).eps rather than a constant. Open question the multi-member run answers: 2.34e-3 is 2.4x fp16's eps, so a single eps is the wrong model for a 12-block transformer's accumulated rounding - the bound may need a measured multiple.
close_reason: Fixed and verified on 2026-08-13 by witness_check across four members: 4 ok, 0 refused, and a deliberately flipped manifest refused at 0.407 against 0.00391.

title: v3+LoRA: the one axis the DINOv3 verdict never varied
description:
Every DINOv3 run inherited DINOv2's adaptation recipe (six blocks rewritten at 8e-6). The 2026-08-13 interpretation ruled out patch grid (441 patches vs 196 bought 0.0023, inside the floor) and capacity (v3-S+ scored 0.0045 WORSE than v3-S), leaving ADAPTATION as the untested axis behind a -0.038 deficit.

MECHANISM: v3 carries LayerScale (per-channel learned gain, init small) and RoPE; v2 has neither. A backbone rate chosen for v2 is not obviously the right step for v3, and an oversized step on those gammas degrades exactly the fine local structure the per-label table says v3 lost - Baker's -0.115, lateral meniscus -0.077, against effusion -0.014. LoRA freezes gammas, RoPE and base weights bit-identical and confines the update to rank 8.

BONUS PROPERTY: LoRA makes the rate comparable ACROSS encoders where fine-tuning could not - the adapters are zero-init new parameters in both cases, so 5e-4 means the same thing on v2 and v3.
design: lora.sh gains variant/size arguments; run is v3small at 224 (its native read, 104s/epoch, ~21 min for 12 epochs). Control is dinov3_v3small_224_s2026 = 0.8057, same encoder, same read, fine-tuned recipe. Second control is lora_r8_small_336 on DINOv2, which says whether rank 8 carries enough capacity at all.
acceptance_criteria: Near 0.84: the encoder was never the problem, our fine-tuning was destroying it - a finding that applies back to DINOv2 and reopens the committed interpretation. Still near 0.80: the representation verdict hardens and the scope caveat closes.
notes: FINAL 2026-08-13: best 0.8217 at epoch 9 of 12, against fine-tuned v3's best 0.8057. +0.0160, three times the 0.0053 floor - better than the interim +0.0136.
close_reason: CONFIRMED and measured: v3+LoRA reaches 0.8217 against fine-tuned v3's 0.8057, +0.0160, three times the floor, and ahead at every matched epoch. The hypothesis was right - DINOv3's deficit was PARTLY our adaptation recipe, and freezing the base (gammas, RoPE, patch embedding, norms) recovers about a third of it. It does not overturn the DINOv2 verdict: 0.819 is still 0.027 short of 0.8457. Recorded in the interpretation and the ledger. The contrast with DINOv2, where the same method is BEHIND at every matched epoch, is the finding: our recipe is right for v2 and wrong for v3.

title: The three-group entry FITS: 1708 units/study against 4140 that already completed
description:
2026-08-12 15:46Z. The last entry died on a resource limit nobody had computed (knee OOM, fusion v2 -> 0.500), so this one is costed before it is built.

THE UNIT is one 336-px image-forward through a 384-wide encoder. A member's cost per study is (slices if whole-stack else 3 x windows) x slots, scaled by (read/336)^2 for pixels and by width/384 for the encoder:

  wsfold0_e6              72     whole-stack, 6 slots
  sliceattn_s2026         72
  slices16_ws_s2026       96     16 cached slices
  lr5x_d6_s2026          180     windowed, 10 overlapping windows
  max12_s2026            180
  max20_s2026            324     20 slices windowed
  large_deep_rank24      486     180 images x 2.7 for a 1024-wide encoder
  res392_ws_s2026         98     72 x (392/336)^2
  intensity392_ws_s2026   98
  extended (9 slots)     108
  TOTAL                 1708 units/study

THE ENTRY THAT COMPLETED, for scale: 23 windowed members x 180 = 4140 units/study, and that is the all-small assumption — if the published members are base it was 8280. So a THREE-GROUP entry with everything we own costs 2.4x LESS than one that already ran inside the limit.

COMPUTE IS THEREFORE NOT THE CONSTRAINT, and that inverts the question: we are not choosing members to fit a budget, we are choosing them because the curve says more than five stops helping (0.8601 at five, 0.8596 at six, 0.8590 at eight). Diversity is the scarce thing, not time.

WHAT IS STILL UNCOSTED: decode. Three pixel groups is three passes over the test set at roughly 1 s/study each in the preview run, so ~75 minutes for a 1,500-study hidden set against a 9-hour limit. Comfortable, and it is the number to re-check if a fourth group ever appears.

MEMORY IS SEPARATELY HANDLED: the forward is now bounded by IMAGE_BUDGET scaled by encoder width (864 for small, 324 for large), which is what the fusion v2 OOM cost us.
notes:
AN ALL-OURS ENTRY IS PACKAGED AND COSTED, 2026-08-13, using this bead's own unit model. It sits at D:/data/.../all_ours (512 MB, 6 members), built with no GPU and no slot.

    member                units/study
    res392_ws                      98
    intensity392_ws                98
    calibrated_targets             72
    sliceattn                      72
    extended_ws                   108
    lora_r8_v3small_224            32
    TOTAL                         480

480 against the 1,708 this bead judged would fit, and against 4,140 that ALREADY COMPLETED on the T4. Eight and a half times the headroom, so neither OOM nor timeout is a live risk. It is that cheap for the same reason the efficiency entry is: a whole-stack member reads ONE window (72 units) where a windowed member costs 180.

WHY THESE SIX. The leaderboard evidence says DIVERSITY beats member quality - a third member of our own recipe bought nothing while a different recipe bought +0.006 - so they are chosen to differ by MECHANISM rather than by score. They differ on five axes at once:
    read size      336 / 392 / 224
    slot scheme    6 slots / 9 slots (extended sees 83,297 slices no other member can reach)
    pooling        max / attend
    encoder        DINOv2-small / DINOv3-small (a different pretraining family)
    supervision    standard / calibrated / intensity-jittered
Three decode groups, which is exactly the three-group case this bead costed.

WHY IT MATTERS NOW: the field moved. The median rose 0.021 in two days while our best rose 0.006, so we fell from the 34th percentile to the 31st while gaining. And none of the whole-stack or 392 px work - about +0.021 offline - has ever been on the board; our best entry is still the mostly-grafted fusion.

STILL GATED on the offline curve (knee-uff), which must be re-run under midranks before it can rank subsets. The package existing is not permission to submit it.

title: Cached-embedding harness: a frozen-encoder proxy that makes a head experiment cost seconds
description:
THE ARITHMETIC. Whole-stack fold-0 is 4,407 studies x 6 slots x 12 slices = 317k images. Encoding them ONCE at the measured 940 img/s is ~5.6 minutes, and 317k x 384 dims x 4 bytes = 487 MB — it fits in RAM, let alone on disk. After that, training the head alone is a few matrix multiplies per epoch: SECONDS, against 320 s now.

WHAT IT BUYS. Every question that does not change the pixels or the encoder becomes ~free to ask: slot-head design, the anatomical prior, rank weight, weight floor, loss shape, slice pooling over cached per-slice vectors, report supervision weight, slot attention. Those are currently 66-minute arms each and they are exactly the class the ledger says returns ~0.005 — a knob-sized answer for an hour of card time. At seconds each they can be swept instead of chosen.

WHAT IT IS NOT. It is a PROXY, not the model: a frozen encoder is a different function from one whose top six blocks adapt, and a head tuned on frozen features may not transfer. THE HARNESS IS ONLY WORTH BUILDING IF THAT CORRELATION IS MEASURED FIRST — take three head variants whose fine-tuned scores we already know, run them frozen, and check the ORDERING survives. If it does not, the harness answers a different question than the one we ask and should be dropped rather than trusted.

WHY NOW. It also unblocks the thing the ledger keeps asking for: the metric rewards diverse members, and a cached-embedding harness can fit dozens of heads on the same features in minutes. Head diversity is weaker than encoder diversity, but it is nearly free, and 'nearly free' is a different budget line from 'an hour each'.

COST TO BUILD: one encode pass writing a memmap keyed like StudyCache (size, slices, scheme, variant), plus a Trainer path that reads vectors instead of pixels. The slot/mask plumbing already exists and is shared.
notes:
THE CONSUMER IS BUILT, 2026-08-13: kneemri/head_trial.py. EmbeddingCache was written by build_embeddings and READ BY NOBODY - a whole corpus encoded and consumed by nothing, the recorded-but-unread shape at cache scale.

HeadTrial pools cached per-slice features by the elementwise max, zeroes absent slots, and fits SlotHead alone with the same objective and head rate the pixel trainer uses. Batch 64 rather than 12: nothing here holds encoder activations, and the ranking term scores pairs WITHIN a batch so a wider one sees quadratically more.

Tested without a GPU: a signal planted in the features is recovered (0.7+) against noise, so the harness can rank head variants at all. If it could not, it would rank nothing and be worth dropping.

WHAT REMAINS AND IT IS THE GATE THIS BEAD SET: the correlation check. Build the cache (one ~6 minute encode), then run head variants whose FINE-TUNED scores we already know and confirm the ORDERING survives. A frozen encoder is a different function from one whose last blocks adapt; until that ordering is measured this harness answers a different question than the one we ask. Needs the GPU for the encode only.

title: Wire a v3 member through to a submission: kit rebuild, dataset_sources, witness
description:
The encoder side is done (knee-8hn). What remains is untested because no v3 member exists yet.

1. THE KIT. comp/kit/kneemri_src is a built copy and still holds the old find_dinov2. It must be rebuilt before any kernel runs a v3 member, or the kernel will not find the mount it now has.
2. DATASET_SOURCES. Every kernel-metadata.json lists model_sources for the two DINOv2 mounts. A v3 entry needs 'dimiturnt/dinov3-hf' in dataset_sources instead — it is a dataset, not a Kaggle model.
3. THE WITNESS. The refuse path has never been exercised against a real member (knee-qws), and a v3 member is the first one whose encoder differs from the training default, so it is the strongest test the gate will ever get.
4. ACKNOWLEDGEMENT. The DINOv3 licence requires acknowledging the materials in any published result, so the README must carry it if a v3 member ever scores.
notes: 2026-08-13: gated on the diversity curve, not on the encoder question. DINOv3 is refuted as an improvement (-0.038 mean, deficit concentrated in Baker's/menisci/contusion) and is a member candidate only. Wire it only if member_curve puts it in the winning subset.

title: Submission budget: gate every entry behind the offline member curve
description:
2026-08-12 06:55Z, at the owner's instruction to start saving submissions.

STATE: 3 of today's 5 spent (3-member, 1-member solo, 23-member fusion). Two left. No auto-submitter is armed - checked; the only background waiters are training queues.

THE MECHANICS, stated because 'saving up' does not mean what it sounds like:
  - 5 submissions per day, reset 00:00 UTC. UNUSED SLOTS DO NOT ROLL OVER, so nothing accumulates by abstaining. Saving only avoids waste.
  - Only TWO Final Submissions are judged (rule 2.2.b). Those are the scarce resource, and they are chosen at the deadline - not automatically the last two submitted.

THE GATE, from now on: no entry is submitted until it has been justified OFFLINE. kneemri.member_curve scores every subset of members on the shared fold-0 holdout and costs no slot; every arm is fitted on that same split, so every candidate ensemble is rankable before it is submitted. Submit only when
  (a) the offline number predicts a gain over our best LB (0.888), or
  (b) the question cannot be answered offline at all - i.e. holdout-to-LB transfer for a recipe that has never been on the board.

WHY THIS IS NOW AFFORDABLE, where it was not yesterday: the member-count curve (knee-9pl) is measured, so we no longer need the leaderboard to tell us that more members help. The remaining open question - WHICH members - is exactly what the offline curve answers.

WHAT IS PENDING AND MUST BE READ BEFORE ANY NEW SPEND: the 3-member entry and the 23-member fusion entry. Fusion in particular sets the top of the count curve and decides whether mixing the published members with ours is worth keeping.
notes:
THE GATE WORKED, 2026-08-15, and it refused an entry I had been ready to argue for. The 24-member fusion - our two best-on-paper members finally admitted after the read-group fix - prices at +0.0001 over the 22-member shape on 48 fold-0 holdout studies. This bead exists to stop slots being spent on 'maybe it is better', and that is exactly what it did: yesterday's verified, fingerprint-checked, kernel-tested entry does not clear the bar.

Also worth recording as evidence this bead's premise is right: our FIRST two members buy +0.022 over the published twenty and the next two buy nothing, so the marginal value of a member collapses fast and enthusiasm about a member's own holdout number is not a substitute for pricing the ENSEMBLE it joins.

title: DINOv3 is permitted by the rules and blocked only by a license click
description:
2026-08-12 06:25Z.

RULES VERDICT (comp/COMPETITION_RULES.txt, saved verbatim). Not banned.
  2.6.b  external data and models are acceptable unless the Host prohibits them, subject to 'reasonably accessible to all' and 'minimal cost'. DINOv3 is free and every participant can obtain it on identical terms - a license click on a free HF account. Passes both tests.
  2.5.a  explicitly contemplates 'pretrained models with an incompatible license' and does NOT require an open-source grant for them.
  3.6.c  constrains open source CODE, not model weights; 2.5.a is the specific provision for weights.

STATE: the HF token at D:/life/creds/machine/hfpat.txt is VALID (account mitkoTrz, read scope). The repos still 403 because the ACCOUNT has not accepted Meta's DINOv3 license. That is an agreement for the owner to accept, not the agent: https://huggingface.co/facebook/dinov3-vits16-pretrain-lvd1689m -> 'Agree and access repository'.

WHY IT IS WORTH A RUN. Published benchmarking (arxiv 2509.06467) finds DINOv3 beats medical-specific foundation models (BiomedCLIP, CT-Net) on several medical tasks despite natural-image-only pretraining, which also deflates knee-zkz's 'swap to a medical encoder' plan. DINOv3 is a straight upgrade of the encoder we already use rather than a domain gamble.

CHEAP TO TRY: patch 16 divides our 336 px cache exactly (336 = 16 x 21), so no re-decode is needed - only an entry in ENCODERS and a train run.

TWO THINGS TO SETTLE BEFORE IT COULD WIN, neither blocking the experiment:
  1. The scored kernel has no internet, so the weights must be mounted from a Kaggle dataset. Kaggle carries only community re-uploads of DINOv3, no official metaresearch mirror; uploading our own copy is a Meta-license redistribution question.
  2. Winner obligation 2.8 wants the final weights as a public Kaggle dataset. For a DINOv3-derived model that means publishing OUR fine-tuned weights, which 2.5.a's carve-out addresses for licensing but Meta's terms govern for derivatives.

DO NOT use a third-party mirror to skip the license click: rule 3.14.a warrants that a Submission infringes no third-party IP, and the click is free.
notes:
2026-08-13 — CAPACITY IS REFUTED TOO. DINOv3 sits at ~0.80 whatever we vary.

  v3small @336   0.8080   441 patches, 1.5x native
  v3small @224   0.8057   196 patches, native resolution
  v3splus @224   0.8012   28.7M parameters against 21.6M, same everything else
  DINOv2-small   0.8457   control

Three runs, spanning a 2.25x range in tokens and a 33% range in parameters, land within 0.007 of each other and 0.045 below the control. Read size does not explain the gap (both directions tried) and neither does student size — S+ is if anything slightly WORSE than S, comfortably inside the floor.

WHAT IS LEFT is that our adaptation recipe was fitted around DINOv2 and does not transfer: 8e-6 on six unfrozen blocks suits an encoder whose blocks are already close to what the task wants, and v3 is a distilled model with RoPE and LayerScale. The owner ruled out spending card time self-tuning that rate, which is the right call — a rate sweep is our hyperparameters, not the data.

SO DINOv3 STOPS HERE AS A LEVER and continues as a MEMBER. 0.8057 is our weakest checkpoint by a distance and the only one from a different encoder family; it reads 224 off the 336 cache, so it shares that decode and costs nothing extra to serve. It is in the diversity curve, which is the only thing that can say whether failing differently is worth 0.04 of individual score.
close_reason: Done: licence accepted, weights mirrored as private dataset dimiturnt/dinov3-hf, three v3 arms trained and scored.

title: The 0.0062 noise floor is holdout SAMPLING error - more seeds cannot lower it
description:
MEASURED 2026-08-12 06:08Z, kneemri.label_power over report_labels_v2.csv.

Hanley-McNeil standard error per label, on an 881-study holdout (one fold of five):

  Fracture          62 positives   SE 0.0311   95% +/-0.061
  Synovitis        116             SE 0.0230   95% +/-0.045
  MCL              153             SE 0.0202   95% +/-0.040
  ...
  Effusion         533             SE 0.0126   95% +/-0.025

  mean of 12       SE 0.0053

THE PREDICTED FLOOR IS 0.0053 AND THE MEASURED SEED SPREAD IS 0.0062. They agree. The floor is therefore not mainly initialisation variance - it is the sampling error of the holdout itself.

FOUR CONSEQUENCES.
1. Multi-seed cannot lower this floor. Averaging seeds removes seed variance, which is the SMALL part; the holdout stays the same 881 studies with the same 62 Fractures. This independently supports the standing ban on seed work, on a mechanism rather than a preference.
2. Any arm delta below ~0.006 is not measurable on this holdout, whatever it does to the model. That is not a statement about the method, it is the resolution of the instrument.
3. Per-label deltas need +/-0.03 to +/-0.06 error bars. Every per-label claim made so far was quoted without one, and two of them shaped a plan (knee-70w, knee-1dw).
4. The project's 1.5% bar is about 3x the floor, which is why it is the right bar and should not be relaxed.

WHAT WOULD ACTUALLY IMPROVE PRECISION: more held-out studies per evaluation, i.e. a LARGER holdout fraction, which trades training data for measurement precision - or accepting the mean as the only readable number and never planning on a single label. The second is free.
close_reason: Closed

title: Cut folds 2-3: k-fold was spending GPU that three untested mechanisms were waiting on
description:
2026-08-11 20:40Z. wholestack_folds.running.sh was running folds 1-2-3 sequentially, ~70 min each.

WHAT FOLD 1 BOUGHT AND FOLDS 2-3 DID NOT. Fold 1 (0.8505 against fold 0's 0.8457) turned whole-stack from a single-seed number into a replicated one AND gave a second ensemble member - that is the 'harden a number that already works' case. Folds 2-3 buy only ensemble variance reduction: they answer no question, and the standing rule is that k-fold is a PERFECTING tool, not a finding tool.

Against that, resolution (448 px), slice_attention and 16-slice whole-stack were all unrun, and each tests a mechanism that could plausibly clear the 1.5% bar.

WHAT WAS DONE: killed the parent script (PID 146626) and deliberately left fold 2's trainer (150098) alive - it was 4/12 epochs in and lands a third ensemble member for tonight's remaining submission slots. Fold 3 never starts.

THE CONSEQUENCE THAT NEEDED CODE: a completion marker is written by run_train in the arm's SHELL, so a trainer outliving its shell never announces itself. after.sh grew a pid:<n> gate for exactly this (commit 9bc4052). Second choice by design - a PID says a process ended, never that it succeeded, so the fold 2 checkpoint must be verified before it is packaged.
close_reason:
DONE AT THE TIME AND OVERTAKEN SINCE. The bead's own body records the action as completed on 2026-08-11 - parent script killed, fold 2 deliberately left to finish as a third member, fold 3 never started - and the after.sh pid gate it required landed in commit 9bc4052.

Overtaken as well: the owner has since BANNED folds and seeds outright (2026-08-12, 'seeds and folds - its the same thing, tried slightly differently'), so 'cut folds 2-3' is no longer a decision this project can face. Nothing here is actionable.

title: publish.py exists because 'the kaggle CLI cannot run here' - that premise is now false
description:
FOUND 2026-08-11 while trying to submit, and it cost the first attempt.

WHAT publish.py SAYS IN ITS OWN DOCSTRING: 'the official kaggle CLI authenticates with a username + key pair, which is a different credential from the KGAT_* access token this project holds, so the documented kaggle datasets version / kaggle kernels push flow cannot run here at all. The REST endpoints take the bearer token directly.'

That justified an entire hand-rolled module: a three-step dataset upload protocol, a kernel push, and a bearer-token auth path.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE NOW:
  - ~/.kaggle/access_token holds a KGAT_* token that EXPIRED ON 2026-07-23, nineteen days ago. credentials.json records access_token_expiration: 2026-07-23T19:17. Kaggle answers an expired bearer token with its marketing HTML rather than a 401, so publish.py fails with a wall of HTML and exit 1 - which is what happened tonight.
  - ~/.kaggle/kaggle.json holds a username + key pair which AUTHENTICATES FINE. KaggleApi().authenticate() returns OK as dimiturnt and lists our three submissions.

So the credential publish.py was written to avoid is the one that works, and the one it was written to use is dead.

WHAT WAS DONE INSTEAD, tonight: the official CLI, which pushed both datasets and the kernel without trouble. One Windows quirk worth writing down - kaggle datasets version -p comp/members fails with a mangled temp path ('comp/members_manifest.json.json') because the CLI concatenates directory and filename; running from inside comp/ with -p members works.

THE DECISION THIS NEEDS, and it is not obvious:
  (a) refresh the KGAT token (credentials.json carries a refresh_token) and keep publish.py, which has the drift gate wired into it - _refuse_if_stale runs before authentication, and that gate has real value;
  (b) retire publish.py for the CLI and move the staleness gate into prepare_submission.sh, which already calls verify_kit;
  (c) keep both and document which to use when.
I would not delete publish.py reflexively: its VALUE was never the transport, it was refusing to publish a stale kit. That belongs somewhere regardless of which client pushes the bytes.

NOT URGENT - the CLI path works and is now proven end to end. But the docstring is actively misleading, which is worse than an absent one.
close_reason: Closed

title: torch.compile and bf16: the last throughput levers, and why they must land at a boundary
description:
AUDIT 2026-08-11 of what we do and do not use, prompted by the owner asking directly.

IN USE:
  - Gradient checkpointing (--recompute-activations, added today). MEASURED: 32 GB -> 19 GB with the loss untouched, and it is what let the whole-stack arm fit at all.
  - SDPA fused attention - already on by default under transformers 5.15 (_attn_implementation reports 'sdpa'), so attention matrices are never materialised. Checked before assuming.

NOT IN USE:
  - bf16. We run fp16 autocast plus a GradScaler, which is autocast's CUDA default rather than a decision anyone made.
  - torch.compile. Nowhere in the tree.
  - TF32. Never set.

WHAT EACH IS WORTH, on this hardware and this loop:
  - bf16: SAME matmul throughput as fp16 on Blackwell. The win is robustness - no GradScaler, no scale-collapse - not speed. We have seen no NaN trouble, so this is insurance rather than a fix.
  - TF32: affects fp32 matmuls only, and under autocast the encoder already runs fp16. Near zero here.
  - torch.compile: the ONLY remaining double-digit lever. 10-30% is typical for a ViT. Compatible with our checkpointing because use_reentrant=False was chosen deliberately.

RISKS FOR COMPILE, to check rather than assume: the final batch of an epoch is partial, so the shape change triggers a recompilation every epoch unless batches drop_last or pad; and the supervised() two-readout path returns a tuple from one encoder pass, which is exactly the sort of graph that can force a break.

WHY NONE OF THIS LANDS MID-QUEUE: every control in the ledger - the 0.8272 baseline, arm Q at 0.8310, the whole-stack arm now running against them - was measured under fp16 with eager kernels. Changing precision or kernel fusion changes numerics, so an arm run afterwards is no longer strictly matched to the control it is quoted against. This project has already paid for one unmatched comparison when a 'new best' turned out to be a seed change.

THE PROTOCOL: land them together at a natural boundary, then run ONE matched arm (same fold, same seed, same recipe) under the new settings and confirm the score is unchanged within the 0.0062 noise floor. If it moves, the speed is not worth an unexplained score change. Record the seconds-per-epoch delta in experiments/README.md so the cost of the guarantee is visible.

Pairs with knee-5f0 (the batch/VRAM sweep): both are throughput work that must be measured on an idle card, and both should be done in one sitting rather than trickled in.
notes: OUTCOME 2026-08-13: both landed and both shipped a defect the audit did not predict. This bead worried about recompilation on the partial final batch (handled: batches drops it) and a graph break in the two-readout path (did not occur). What it missed was that torch.compile REBOUND over the module attribute, renaming every state-dict key to backbone._orig_mod.* and making five members unloadable - knee-5he. And bf16's arrival made the inference autocast's missing dtype a live bug, knee-5qt, plus put the witness tolerance below bf16's own epsilon, knee-6pi. All three are filed and fixed; closing this as the audit it was.
close_reason: Both levers landed (compile -21% at batch 2 measured, bf16 in use). The three defects they brought are filed separately as knee-5he, knee-5qt, knee-6pi.

title: Give VRAM back to the other project: find the smallest batch that still saturates compute
description:
OWNER'S FRAMING, 2026-08-11, and it is the right one: VRAM is a HARD partition (oversubscribe it and Windows pages over PCIe, which is how a 32 GB run ended up at 145 W of 575 doing nothing), while compute is time-sliced. So the objective is the SMALLEST memory footprint that still saturates the SMs - the free space is worth real money to the other project on this card, and the utilisation is shared anyway.

WHERE WE ARE, measured under whole-stack at batch 12 with checkpointing and an 18 GB cap:
  VRAM 19.2 GB | utilisation 95-100% | power 540-556 W of 575 (96%) | CPU 12%
That is COMPUTE-limited, unambiguously. A memory-limited run looks like the uncapped version of the same arm: 100% 'utilisation' at 145 W with 1% memory-controller traffic.

THE SWEEP, to run when the GPU is free: batch 12 / 8 / 6 / 4 at fixed everything else, recording peak VRAM, power, utilisation and seconds per epoch. Expected shape - VRAM falls sublinearly because weights, optimiser states, CUDA context and the checkpoint boundaries are fixed costs, so batch 6 lands near 12-13 GB rather than 9.6; power and utilisation hold until the batch gets small enough to go launch-bound.

MUST BE MEASURED ALONE. A second process on the card time-shares the SMs, so both would report ~100% utilisation and the reading would say nothing about either.

THE CAVEAT THAT STOPS THIS BEING A FREE KNOB: batch size is not neutral to the OBJECTIVE. The ranking term scores pairs WITHIN a batch - 66 pairs at batch 12, 15 at batch 6 - so shrinking the batch weakens the exact term we added deliberately. Any batch chosen for memory reasons has to be re-measured on score, not assumed equivalent. The lever that IS free is gradient checkpointing, already applied: 32 GB -> 19 GB with the loss untouched.

OUTPUT: a recommended (batch, vram-gb) pair per arm shape, recorded in experiments/README.md so arms declare a budget rather than taking what they find.
notes:
TWO THINGS MEASURED TODAY THAT CHANGE HOW THIS SHOULD BE RUN, neither of which needs the card.

1. THE CAP DOES NOT PARTITION THE DEVICE. --vram-gb bounds PYTORCH'S ALLOCATOR, and driver context plus kernel workspaces sit on top of it. Set to 30 on a 32.6 GB card it left no headroom and Windows paged GPU memory over PCIe rather than raising OOM: the run crawled at 40 img/s against ~1000, reporting 100% utilisation, 1.75 hours per epoch. A cap only converts thrashing into a clean OOM if it leaves the driver its room, and set too high it PERMITS the thrashing it exists to prevent. 26 is what every healthy arm uses. So 'VRAM is a hard partition' is true of the device and NOT of the number in the flag - the flag is a soft bound with an unmodelled overhead on top, which is exactly the thing this sweep is trying to calibrate.

2. expandable_segments IS A NO-OP ON THIS MACHINE. Torch prints 'expandable_segments not supported on this platform' at startup on Windows. Three arms carried it and none was helped; any fragmentation it was credited with reclaiming was never reclaimed. Do not include it as a variable in the sweep, and do not credit a result to it.

AND A CAVEAT ON THE SWEEP AS DESIGNED: batch 12 / 8 / 6 / 4 does not hold the objective fixed. The ranking term scores pairs WITHIN a batch - 66 at batch 12 against 15 at batch 6 - so a smaller batch is a different loss, not merely a smaller memory footprint. The sweep answers 'what fits' honestly and 'what scores' only if --rank-weight 0 is used, or if the score is read as confounded.

title: Runs are compared by grepping logs: no metrics file, no experiment tracker
description:
RAISED BY THE OWNER 2026-08-11, asking about mlflow/tqdm/periodic logging.

WHAT LANDED IMMEDIATELY: kneemri/heartbeat.py. One line per epoch could not distinguish a slow run from a wedged one, and that cost a quarter of an hour today - a whole-stack arm sat thrashing on a VRAM overflow and the only evidence was the card's power draw. The heartbeat reports step, loss and images/s every 30 seconds, paced by SECONDS because step cost varies ~20x across arms.

TQDM WAS CONSIDERED AND REJECTED, on a specific ground rather than taste: every arm's output is redirected to a file. A progress bar in a file is a trail of carriage returns - the HuggingFace weight-loading bar already litters every log we own, and it is the reason grepping arm logs needs a 'grep -v Loading weights'. A log line is the right instrument when the reader is a file, not a terminal.

WHAT IS STILL MISSING, and what it costs: there is no machine-readable record of a run. Comparing arms today means grepping 'best holdout' out of a dozen log files scattered across /tmp and processed/experiments, by hand, and the ledger in experiments/README.md is maintained by ME rather than by the runs. That is how a result gets misattributed - it already happened once, when a 'new best' turned out to be a seed change.

THE CHEAP FIX, and the one I would do first: a metrics.jsonl beside each checkpoint - one line per epoch with {epoch, loss, auc, seconds, lr, vram_peak}. No server, no daemon, nothing to run; it is greppable, diffable, and plots from pandas in three lines. Data stays out of the repo like every other artefact.

ON MLFLOW SPECIFICALLY: it would give run comparison and a UI, and it costs a local server plus a tracking directory plus a dependency, and it wants to own the run lifecycle. For a single-machine project whose arms are already committed shell scripts, that is a lot of machinery for what a JSONL and pandas provide. I would only reach for it if we start running many arms per day and need to slice them by hyperparameter interactively. Worth revisiting then, not now.

NOT URGENT while the queue is one arm deep - it is a workflow cost, not a score cost.
close_reason: Closed
